reden: Yes. The report explicitly flags that the Safe’s setFallbackHandler is not blocked by the Guard, and explains that calls routed through the Safe fallback bypass checkTransaction/isRentedOut. It further calls out the exact ERC1155 creation-time vector: Seaport uses safeTransferFrom, onERC1155Received is routed to the attacker-chosen fallback handler before validateOrder/addRentals registers the rental, enabling the renter to drain the 1155 during that window. This matches the described exploit mechanism (custom fallback handler + onERC1155Received reentrancy before rental registration) and the same code path (FallbackManager.fallback → handler.onERC1155Received, with registration in Create/_rentFromZone/AddRentals lagging). Blocking/restricting setFallbackHandler as per the report would also prevent the described hijack. Therefore the audit report detected the same vulnerability.
